nemesis.title: Counter-Strike: Team Nemesis vs 1WIN - Map 2 Winner

officialMatch.note: The committed Polymarket rule says an unfinished Map 2 resolves 50-50. The committed closed market metadata has both tokens at 0.5 and no winner.

nemesis.marketRule: If Map 2 is not completed for any reason, this market will resolve 50-50.

findings: The M80 burst began in a publicly visible 9-6, planted-bomb, five-versus-three state; it was not advance knowledge of the round result.
Most M80 notional was passive: the target absorbed opposite-outcome takers after the market repriced.
The 1WIN forfeit case lost money and resolved 50-50, falsifying an always-correct or indiscriminate late-CS2 interpretation.
Reverse breadth is not a standalone edge: 4/9 historical clusters produced -73.5% ROI.
The remaining CS2 hypothesis is state selection plus liquidity provision, not breadth or speed alone.
limits: Broadcast timestamps include stream delay and do not reveal the target's source.
One profitable M80 case cannot establish a strategy win rate.
The M80 state observation was assembled after the result and is a mechanism audit, not a prospective backtest.
